title: Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles mayor over incumbent Karen Bass
description: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman has toppled incumbent Karen Bass in the race for mayor of Los Angeles.Raman's win stunned political watchers in Cali
body: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman has toppled incumbent Karen Bass in the race for mayor of Los Angeles.Raman's win stunned political watchers in California after she entered the race as a long-shot candidate against Bass, a political heavyweight who previously served in Congress and had never lost a race for political office. Raman has frequently been compared to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Both are democratic socialists and ran on progressive platforms. Her win solidifies that America's two biggest cities will now be led by democratic socialists, which include some of the most high-profile politicians in the US, such as Mamdani and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.Los Angeles was always likely to have a Democratic mayor but the question in the city - the second most populous city in the US - was just how left voters would be willing to go.Bass, also Democrat, announced that she had called and conceded to Raman in a post on social media on Thursday, writing "while this is not the outcome we hoped for, the people of Los Angeles have spoken." "Moving this city forward is what Los Angeles needs from all of us," Bass wrote. "I love Los Angeles. I believe in Los Angeles. And I will continue to ensure the promise of a better life belongs to all of us." Boebert, billionaires' tax and other midterms races still to watchFood, fuel and taxes – can the Democrats actually make life cheaper?'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeatRaman, a member of city council and Indian immigrant, ran on a platform of change and fixing the "broken status quo and the politicians who failed them over and over again". She ran on cutting homelessness, increasing housing in the city, saving Hollywood jobs from continued cuts and protecting residents from immigration enforcement efforts. Raman also vowed to fix the city's many issues, including helping beautification efforts, fixing roads and even helping bring back nightlife in the city. The major issue in the race, however, was the LA fires, which killed dozens of people and razed neighbourhoods across the area in 2025. Bass faced intense political fallout over her absence during the emergency and the city's response to the disaster. The next mayor in LA will oversee hosting the Super Bowl in 2027 and the 2028 Summer Olympics.

schema.headline: Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles mayor over incumbent Karen Bass

title: Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel?
description: The warnings came in thick and fast, targeting one airline or airport after another. In nearly all cases - London's Heathrow airport being a notable e
body: The warnings came in thick and fast, targeting one airline or airport after another. In nearly all cases - London's Heathrow airport being a notable exception - they were taken to be credible enough to divert the aircraft in question, or even in Italy's case, to scramble fighter jets to escort it. They all turned out to be false, which does not, of course, mean that the next ones will not  be real.It is hardly surprising that the simultaneous, co-ordinated nature of these airline hoaxes, coupled with other malicious actions across Europe, are causing some people to point the finger of suspicion at Russia. Following a series of cyber-attacks and mysterious drone sightings over sensitive sites earlier this year, in the past few days we have seen the remote hacking of supermarket freezers, as well as a blood bank, a suspicious incident on Poland's border with Russia, and in August a drone attack Germany's Leipzig Halle airport which its interior minister publicly blamed on Moscow.So is Russia behind this?There are many who argue, based purely on circumstantial evidence, that this must surely be yet another example of "hybrid", "grey zone" or "sub-threshold" warfare - actions that damage a nation's infrastructure or society but which tend to be anonymous, deniable and which fall short of triggering Nato's Article 5 and thereby mobilising a response by the West.Moscow is certainly furious with Nato for supporting Ukraine and, in doing so, frustrating the Kremlin's plans to swallow up that country and effectively terminate its independence. Russian bloggers have also suggested that, if Ukraine's drones are currently making Russia's airports unsafe, and Western sanctions are blocking Russian airlines from European airspace, then why shouldn't Western nations feel the same pain?But as of Thursday evening no hard evidence had emerged linking the airline hoaxes to Russia, Iran or any proxy groups controlled by them. There is the email threat sent on Thursday morning to airport authorities in Rome, purporting to be from "Fighters of the Male State". That name likely refers to the Russian group Muzhskoi Legion or "Male Legion", an ultra-right group with such extreme views it was banned by a Moscow court in 2021. Yet, it retained tens of thousands of online followers on Telegram as it cheered on the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in the following year.But the email sent to Rome, even if genuine - and who is to say it is not another group hiding behind that name? - is unlikely to provide the leads that police and airport authorities need to pin down who is generating these hoaxes and why.For national police forces, airport authorities and transport ministries trying to work out who is behind these hoaxes and how best to mitigate their effect when they happen again, the task is not to go with who they think might be the most likely culprits but instead to follow the cold, hard leads - if they can find them.

schema.headline: Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel?

title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
description: US First Lady Melania Trump called for a "more enduring" ceasefire in Ukraine as she welcomed Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House fol
body: US First Lady Melania Trump called for a "more enduring" ceasefire in Ukraine as she welcomed Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House following last week's truce in the southern region of Kherson.Hundreds of residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky facing starvation and constant bombardment were able to evacuate during a six-day ceasefire, which both Moscow and Kyiv credited Trump with brokering."The lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace," she said.The unusual White House event saw senior Ukrainian and Russian officials meet away from the setting of official US-brokered peace talks they have been holding without success since last year.The delegations were made up of Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, as well as Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev.Melania Trump was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire, and all parties conveyed to her the gratitude of the Russian and Ukrainian presidents.The US first lady said she had "reviewed demining plans, aerial images, assessed roadways, and discussed evacuation routes, hospital access, vehicles, and medical resources" during the truce."Last week in Oleshky and neighbouring areas of Kherson, people experienced the simple joys of life for the first time since 2022," Trump said. "They walked down familiar streets without fear of explosions."She thanked both Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin, making no reference to the origins of the war, which began when the Russian president launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and which has caused thousands of civilian casualties and the displacement of millions. Dmitriev, a businessman and Kremlin special envoy who has previously represented Moscow during peace talks with Ukraine, thanked Trump for "saving and touching so many lives"."Let us continue making a humanitarian contribution together; this is within our power," Dmitriev said, before gifting Melania Trump a framed drawing by an 11-year-old Oleshky evacuee.He also praised Trump for her work on reuniting children separated from their families by the war. These include children allegedly abducted by Russia.Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads Zelensky's party in parliament who has also been part of the Ukrainian negotiating team, said the Oleshky ceasefire had constituted the "biggest de-escalation since 2022"."We are creating a momentum where both sides are learning the… mechanics of how to actually keep the peace when the peace comes," he added. He acknowledged that the "political track" of negotiations to end the conflict was "complex" but said Ukrainians were asking Melania Trump "to keep going and find new missions and de-escalate more."At the end of the event, Trump  handed Dmitriev and Arakhamia two letters to be hand-delivered to their respective presidents.The White House later said Melania Trump had invited her guests to view two historic artifacts which she had "personally selected as powerful symbols of peace".One was an 18th Century medicine chest which was removed from the White House when the British set it on fire in 1812. "Once adversaries, the United States and Great Britain ultimately established a strong alliance," the White House said.The second artifact was a cup gifted in 1899 to the French ambassador in recognition of his efforts to bring the Spanish-American war to an end.Melania Trump has generally remained discreet on foreign policy matters, and neither Moscow nor Kyiv have elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement in coordinating the delicate ceasefire - the most enduring and widespread of the war so far.A source who works in the local government of the Kherson region told the BBC that work on the Oleshky evacuation had been ongoing for almost a year. However, the source said, "at a certain point other individuals became involved, seemingly after most of the groundwork had already been laid and subsequently began taking credit for the progress that had been made."It was difficult to determine exactly who had played what role and at which stage of the process, the source acknowledged, adding that "those who had been directly involved in the negotiations for nearly a year were eventually prohibited from communicating publicly about the matter."Speaking after the meeting in the White House had taken place, President Zelensky said the success of the Oleshky ceasefire "had proved a very simple thing: when Putin wants the fighting to stop, it stops.""The same applies to our people who are held in Russian captivity. When Putin wants, they go home."A source close to American officials shared a similar assessment, implying to the BBC that despite the outward praise, "the person who made [the ceasefire] possible, whether we like it or not, is essentially Putin.""And this was done in order to pass the ball to [Donald] Trump... so that it would have some positive effect for his midterm elections."There has been no change whatsoever in Russia's position, Ukrainian political analyst Dmytro Levus told the BBC. Moscow "agreed to it because there was pressure from the American side... In doing so, the Russians confirmed Zelenskyy's words that, when necessary, it turns out Russia can quickly stop firing and even maintain that ceasefire."As the frontline region of Kherson experienced its first six days of peace in several years, the rest of Ukraine continued to come under Russian attack. This week, several drone and missile attacks killed and injured civilians across the country. On Monday alone, more than 40 people were killed in a single Russian strike on an aid distribution centre in the region of Zaporizhzhia. More are thought to still be buried under the rubble.Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko in Kyiv

schema.headline: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials

title: The Russell Brand I saw in court was not the flamboyant character most people will know
description: In the dock Brand's statue-like demeanour was broken only occasionally, when, during some of the evidence, he closed his eyes for several seconds, per
body: In the dock Brand's statue-like demeanour was broken only occasionally, when, during some of the evidence, he closed his eyes for several seconds, perhaps in silent prayer or meditation. There was no fidgeting or movement. He didn't flinch.He maintained his composure even during some of the most harrowing evidence, when one of the victims told the court how blood and faeces had been left on Brand's bed sheets after he had raped her at his house.During the testimony, Brand let out a sigh and looked at the ceiling with his eyes closed.Speculation grew about whether Brand would give evidence - defendants can choose whether to take to the stand in their trials. It became a daily talking point among the reporters.Giving evidence yourself can be a double-edged sword; a chance to vigorously defend one's innocence on the one hand, balanced by the risk of being torn apart by the prosecution barrister.But it finally happened. Brand took to the witness box on day 10 of the trial. His testimony was perhaps unsurprising - after all, nobody apart from his wife had been prepared to speak up for him in court as part of the defence's case.Brand entered the witness box wearing a dark suit and a white open-necked shirt. It was a nervous beginning. In an unusually loud voice he answered "no" to each of the allegations that were put to him.He had taken his bible oath loudly too and stood, bolt upright with hands clasped behind his back.I watched him like a hawk. This was a TV personality who was very much part of my youth, but now being interrogated with his liberty on the line.His nerves seemed to visibly ease, so much so that at one point he put his hands in his pockets. It was noticeable that after an adjournment, he was back in his ramrod style stance with hands out of his pockets, behind his back.His wife attended court with him every day - soberly dressed, she sometimes took notes when the complainants were giving evidence.Her support for her husband was visible - holding his hand as they walked in, smiling at him while he was in the dock for hours at a time.Brand's minder often sat next to her in the public benches, and her father, former Ryder Cup-winning golfer Bernard Gallacher sat with her in the gallery during the defence closing. Brand's father, Ron, also attended regularly, exchanging polite chat with some of the media.At 51 years of age, Brand looked gaunt and visibly thinner as the trial neared its end, he seemed to have lost weight as the days went on. Other reporters said the same. We discussed whether signs of confidence he showed at the start had slowly ebbed away.The verdicts came on Thursday after the jury had been deliberating for eight hours and 30 minutes.Brand, who stood upright in the dock, showed limited emotion as the verdicts were read out. "Sit down Mr Brand," the judge told him after the verdicts were delivered."On what happens next," he added, "obviously a custodial sentence of some length will result."Brand mouthed "I'm good, I'm good" to his defence counsel as he was led away.But his appearance in court was an extraordinary fall from grace. A man hailed as a multi-media celebrity, a self-confessed ladies' man too, but now a convicted rapist in custody.

schema.headline: The Russell Brand I saw in court was not the flamboyant character most people will know

title: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says
description: The King relishes the "tough parts" of his role and will continue to be used in "politically charged situations", a senior palace aide said at the end
body: The King relishes the "tough parts" of his role and will continue to be used in "politically charged situations", a senior palace aide said at the end of the King's tour of the Caribbean.Over the past nine days, the King visited the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda and has been used as "a great secret weapon", the aide said.Questions over whether the UK should apologise and pay reparations for its role in the transatlantic slave trade were a theme of the visit."I think what we're seeing is a very clear pattern emerging of the government asking the King to head into quite politically charged situations, quite challenging situations," the aide said. "We have to tread quite a careful line sometimes between government policy and the King's role."The leadership of all three countries visited on the Caribbean tour wanted reparatory justice."I would say, in the round, this has been a complex visit. It's been challenging. It's been exhausting," the aide said. "But the takeaway is that it's been very successful and I think the King has demonstrated his statecraft both by word and deed."Most of the King's visits outside the UK have seen him draw on some delicate diplomatic skills on behalf of his government. In the US, he used his speech to Congress to remind President Donald Trump of the UK's value as an ally. A year earlier he made a flying visit to Canada to welcome new Prime Minister Mark Carney as the latter faced an onslaught of threats and insults from Trump. Visits to Germany and France in the early part of the King's reign were designed to establish new UK alliances post-Brexit."The King is not just King for the easy parts of the job, but the tough parts of the job, too," said the aide. "In fact, that's probably the part of the job that he relishes most, whether that's leading on the environment, whether it's renewing and refreshing and reinvigorating relationships with nations where there have been some complex political issues at play, that is what he lives and breathes for."The senior palace aide has worked closely with the King for many years and has a unique insight into his work and what motivates the monarch."He is able to reach the parts that dare I say politicians probably couldn't quite have reached," he said wryly.The intervention of Prime Minister Andy Burnham saying he was open to the UK apologising for its role in the slave trade midway through the Caribbean tour only intensified the conversations.The senior palace aide dismissed any suggestion that Buckingham Palace was surprised, even blindsided, by the shift in the government position saying they were told about it in a "timely manner".English authorities and the monarchy were prominent participants in the centuries-long slave trade which saw millions of Africans enslaved and forced to work, especially on plantations in the Caribbean and the Americas.Asked directly if the King would apologise for slavery, the senior aide laid out the chain of command in a constitutional monarchy."The King is the crown, the crown is the state, the state is run by an elected government, so we have to see how this whole situation plays through."Since the start of his reign in 2022, the King has had four prime ministers - it's been a quick turnover rate with the King having to establish a new relationship each time, helped by their weekly audiences. Those close to the King view his early encounters with Burnham as a positive start."They get on very well. I see them together every week," explained the royal aide. "It genuinely is a good relationship, but as it is with all the prime ministers and all the ex-prime ministers as well."Royal tours may look pretty but they can be gruelling.There were about 40 engagements on this tour - many of them carried out in temperatures of around 35C with stifling humidity.While the King, who is still undergoing treatment for cancer, will be 78 years old next week and the Queen will celebrate her 80th birthday next July, they are both still managing the rigours of royal visits when many of their friends are enjoying retirement."This is literally what he was born to do, he's very good at it, and he enjoys the reaction he gets from people in the doing of it," the aide said.He added the King and Queen's bond after 20 years of marriage helped get them through the trickier sides of their work when things have "gone a bit wonky".Royal tours always throw up those "wonky" moments.In Antigua and Barbuda, at a rally to mark the country's Independence Day, a sudden downpour left the King drenched, without an umbrella and looking momentarily cross."You know sometimes things don't work entirely according to plan, but it was very quickly resolved, and as we saw, he was laughing… he thought it was genuinely funny," the royal aide recalled.And in the Bahamas, the King joined dancers during a Junakanoo, a traditional carnival celebrating the culture of the islands dating back to the days of slavery.In his speech the King spoke of the slave trade as a shameful chapter that filled his heart with sorrow as he delivered his main speech at the Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting.He was addressing a room full of leaders where many wanted him to say sorry, offer reparations or in some cases, be removed as their head of state.The Antiguan Prime Minister, Gaston Browne, hosted the King and Queen but wants major change including moving his country towards becoming a republic.He said he also wanted to see "structured, inclusive dialogue on the enduring consequences of slavery and colonialism".Buckingham Palace knows the direction of travel. In 2021, Barbados removed the British sovereign as head of state. The mood was of a divorce where all parties still want to be friends… if possible. It's given neighbouring countries a taste of a something different."The King and the royal family are there to serve the people of these regions for as long as they wish," the senior royal aide said. "But if they don't wish it anymore, then we really are fully open to that. The family serves when it's wanted and if not, then a new arrangement can be found."

schema.headline: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says

title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
description: Russell Brand has been convicted of rape and sexual assault, and is now expected to face a substantial prison sentence.A jury found the entertainer gu
body: Russell Brand has been convicted of rape and sexual assault, and is now expected to face a substantial prison sentence.A jury found the entertainer guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, following a four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court in London.He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape, and one count of attempted indecent assault. The jury deliberated for eight-and-a-half hours.The 51-year-old was refused bail and will spend the weekend in custody before he is due to return to the same court on Monday for sentencing.It can now be reported that Brand is also facing further rape allegations made by two women and has already been questioned by officers in relation to the complaints. The Metropolitan Police said its investigation "remains ongoing".During the trial, Brand faced allegations from six women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009, when he rose to fame as one of Britain's most high-profile entertainers.The women came to court to reveal how Brand used his immense fame to force them into sexual activity.Brand, who told his wife Laura Brand "I love you" after entering the dock, displayed no emotion as the jury delivered its verdicts.Afterwards he mouthed "I'm good, I'm good" to his defence counsel as he left the dock. His walk was steadily paced, and he continued to show little emotion.The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, told Brand to expect "a significant custodial term" after the verdicts were delivered.After the verdict, Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy paid tribute to the "extraordinary courage, resilience and determination of the women who came forward and reported what happened to them". "Despite intense media and public scrutiny, they relived deeply personal and traumatic experiences and placed their trust in us. Without their bravery, this outcome would not have been possible," he said."Brand used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women. As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement."He added: "I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be."David Roberts, senior crown prosecutor in the London rape and serious sexual assault unit, described Brand as "predatory"."He was a manipulator with an insatiable desire to get what he wanted regardless of whether consent was given or not," he said."As his career took off, he seized opportunities to assault the women around him. Although his tactics varied, at the centre of every assault was an abuse of power and sexual greed, with a complete disregard for the impact of his actions.Ron Brand, Russell's father told the BBC he was "bemused and shocked" by the verdicts, adding: "I just didn't expect this - it's wrong... it's devastating."In his evidence, Brand admitted using his fame to "facilitate sexual access" and being "obsessed" with sex and "extremely promiscuous" in the past.He said he had "dedicated a lot of my life to what seems now beyond reckless, philandering, and idiocy".But he insisted the sex was always consensual, and he denied all the charges.His barrister told jurors that Brand "had an immense amount of sex", but that "none of it was unlawful".Allegations about Brand's behaviour first emerged in the media in September 2023.The Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches programme jointly reported that four women had accused him of rape, sexual assault and emotional abuse - claims he strongly denied.The investigation into other reports against Brand began soon after the story broke.Brand first rose to fame as a stand-up comedian and became a household name as host of TV shows such as Big Brother's Big Mouth, and with his own radio programmes on stations including BBC Radio 2 and 6 Music.He went on to establish a Hollywood career, starring in films including Forgetting Sarah Marshall and Get Him To The Greek. He was married to pop star Katy Perry from 2010 to 2012.In recent years he has reinvented himself as an online social, political and religious commentator.Channel 4, The Times and Sunday Times and the BBC all paid tribute to the women involved in the case, highlighting their "courage".Channel 4, which aired Big Brother and its spin-off programmes at the time Brand was a presenter, said it recognised the "profound impact of these crimes".The Times and The Sunday Times also paid tribute to women who took part in their investigation with Channel 4 but who did not have their cases brought before a court, saying their contributions had been "vital".A BBC spokesperson said there could be "no place for the abuse of power" and added: "Across the industry we must work together to ensure that anyone who suffers at someone else's hand feels able to report it, that their concerns are taken seriously and that they are listened to."The corporation restated its apology to staff who felt they could not speak up with concerns about Brand's behaviour when he worked at the BBC between 2006 and 2008, because he was seen as "too influential".

schema.headline: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault

title: Cristiano Ronaldo retirement: Why has Portugal legend retired from international game?
description: Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him.The Portugal legend has gone another way, an
body: Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him.The Portugal legend has gone another way, and it was always going to be the case.The 41-year-old announced his international retirement after 23 years but also after a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus which was resolved with a sanction of 30 days, that had already been served, and a fine of 255 euros.It was the punishment imposed on the Portuguese striker for leaving the team's training camp without permission. Jesus kept him on the bench for one match and said he did not plan to start him in the next, so Ronaldo went home.His last appearance came on 24 September against Wales. He ends his international career with 146 goals in 234 games.A message went around Portugal with a big thank you for everything, calling Ronaldo a global ambassador and an inspiration to millions. Even so, the way it ended leaves a bit of a bitter taste.Was he going to be named in the next squad? Possibly, as Jesus said the door was open and the decision was Ronaldo's. What is clear is that he was no longer an automatic starter, and Cristiano has never handled that well.So is this another hissy fit? Partly, yes. He reacted the way he always has when a coach questions his place. But the label hides how much he adapted over the years.Such a pattern appears with almost every man who sat on the Portuguese bench - there were clashes, but also communion with managers and team-mates that help explain this ending.When a young Ronaldo first joined the squad, he arrived at camp with his baseball cap on backwards, enormous sunglasses and headphones turned up so loud they could be heard from a distance.He would not take the cap off to eat among veterans like Luis Figo and Rui Costa. Luiz Felipe Scolari saw an extraordinary player who was immature and obsessed with showing off. He reprimanded him in public, then told him privately that if he changed his attitude, he would one day captain Portugal.The first great disappointment came early, and it came at home. At 19, Ronaldo played in the final of Euro 2004 at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, in front of a country that had convinced itself the trophy was already on its way.A single headed goal by Angelos Charisteas was enough for unfancied Greece to win it by surprise. When the final whistle went, Ronaldo could not hold back the tears, and the image of the teenager crying on his own pitch travelled everywhere.It was a painful way to learn what a final costs, and it left him with a hunger that never really went away.Figo owned the number 7 at the time, so Ronaldo had to have 17. Figo helped him settle but had no intention of making it easy. When he left the national team in 2006, the shirt and the team became Ronaldo's.In September 2005, before a qualifier in Russia, Scolari and Figo went to his room to tell him his father had died. Scolari offered to send him home. Ronaldo chose to play, asked his team-mates to behave as normal, and spent time in the dressing room doing ball tricks.That was his way to cope with the expected but still hugely hurtful passing of his alcoholic dad.  He later called Scolari "father". That way the national team had become the place that held him together.Things went sour with Carlos Queiroz. After the 2010 World Cup exit against Spain, asked to explain a poor performance, Ronaldo told journalists to ask the coach. His influence in the camp had grown so large it changed routines and habits, which explains why the coach felt undermined.The sociologist Joao Nuno Coelho offers the best lens on how Portugal sees him. In his analysis, the national team became a representation of Portuguese identity and of the country's need to be seen internationally.In years of economic hardship and a crisis of confidence, a team that won admiration abroad was important beyond football.Ronaldo stood at the centre of that need and created contradictory feelings. Some Portuguese questioned his individualism and his ego, and not everyone saw themselves in his personality.Coelho explains criticising him became more difficult as time went by. The country wanted to be proud of him and sometimes felt uneasy at the same time.The former international Jorge Andrade told me some supporters preferred figures like Figo, Eusebio, Paulo Futre or Rui Costa. Even so, Portugal was proud to have him. And with the titles, the doubts eased.Under Fernando Santos in 2016, he changed. He accepted playing as a centre forward next to Nani - he had never taken a coach's instructions so naturally.After the opening draw with Iceland, he told Nani in private that he trusted Santos, and the dressing room began to see a real captain. After missing a penalty against Austria, he barely slept. Santos woke up and found him already awake.At the training camp in Marcoussis, he took a fan's megaphone and told supporters Portugal had won nothing yet. He was enjoying the leadership role.In the final in Paris, he left the pitch in tears, injured. He had not had the best tournament, with a muscle complaint that did not let him perform at his best.Nani took the armband. At half-time Ronaldo pulled himself together to encourage his team-mates, and before extra time, still limping, he told Eder he would score.And Eder did.But the old instinct never fully disappeared. During extra-time, Ronaldo stood in the technical area giving orders until the fourth official sent him back. Other coaches I consulted found it excessive.His greatest strength, the need to influence every result, also made limits hard to accept.When he debuted in 2003, Portugal was still searching for its first major title. Some players mark an era, and others change a national team for good. He belongs to the second group.That night in July 2016 gave Portugal its first European Championship.Three years later he scored a hat-trick against Switzerland to put them into the first Nations League final, which Portugal won. In 2025 he lifted a second Nations League at an age when most players have retired.No one has scored more goals for a national side, and no one has pulled on the Portugal shirt more times.Under his influence, Portugal stopped being a gifted team and became one that arrives at every tournament expecting to contend, while a whole generation of players came through a dressing room where he decided what the standard was.Coelho's point holds here as well: a small country found a way to be noticed, and for two decades he was its face.After 2016 the question around him changed. Fewer asked whether he was selfish, and more asked whether Portugal depended on him too much.In the World Cup in 2018, he scored three against Spain, including a free-kick after 45 attempts in major tournaments, and the team still went out to Uruguay.After a difficult 2026 World Cup, much was made of him still starting up front when in fact statistically that was his best period.Under Roberto Martinez, with 28 goals in 37 games, 0.756 per match, improves the 0.624 with Santos.The federation has announced a special tribute to honour his contribution, and that is necessary as the exit has not left fans room for a celebration they want to be part of.Not only they grew up with him, he took them to places they had not yet been.

schema.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo retirement: Why has Portugal legend retired from international game?

title: Married at First Sight UK cancelled after BBC revealed rape allegations
description: Married at First Sight UK will not return, Channel 4 has said, following a BBC investigation into the hit reality TV show.The Channel 4 show was plung
body: Married at First Sight UK will not return, Channel 4 has said, following a BBC investigation into the hit reality TV show.The Channel 4 show was plunged into crisis earlier this year, after Panorama revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show, while a third woman alleged a non-consensual sex act. The men involved have denied all the allegations against them.A review was commissioned by Channel 4 shortly after the BBC first contacted the broadcaster, with details of the allegations we had heard.On Thursday, the completed review recommended extra safeguards on the show. But Channel 4 said the programme had "run its course" and apologised to the women involved in the investigation.The broadcaster's chief executive Priya Dogra said she was "very sorry for the distress those women have clearly felt", adding that the show's budget would be reinvested in "distinctive new programming".The Panorama investigation in May, in which three women made allegations about the men they were partnered with - claims the men deny, made the following allegations:One woman said her onscreen husband raped her and threatened her with an acid attack.A second woman told both Channel 4 and CPL, before broadcast, about being allegedly raped by her onscreen husband. Her episodes were still aired.A third woman - Shona Manderson, the only woman who was identified - accused her onscreen husband of sexual misconduct.All three women accused the show of not doing enough to protect them.Lawyers for CPL, the independent production company that makes the UK version of the show, previously said its welfare system is "gold standard" and industry-leading, and that it acted appropriately in all these cases.Channel 4 had initially told Panorama that all the allegations were "wholly uncorroborated".Dame Caroline Dinenage MP, chair of the House of Commons culture and media committee, said the decision to axe the show "makes sense" given the review's findings and the "seriousness of the allegations". "Reality TV contestants have often been treated as a commodity, with duty of care a slogan rather than a genuine principle. Everyone involved in producing and regulating reality TV must now learn and act," she added. A spokesman for Ofcom said the broadcast regulator would "carefully consider the reports published today as we move to strengthen our guidance for broadcasters". "We are clear that broadcasters have a duty of care towards members of the public who participate in their programmes."What is your reaction to the cancellation of MAFS UK?The review into the show was split into two - one part examined welfare protocols on MAFS UK, and the other reported on how Channel 4 handled the allegations.The review into welfare protocols, led by former BBC One Controller Lorraine Heggessey, concluded that some parts of the programme's format increased "the risk profile of the show".Although she found the protocols for MAFS UK were extremely thorough and of a high standard, she said "intimacy is a key focus", and that "some elements of the show could implicitly put pressure on contributors to be intimate".Heggessey made suggestions including installing CCTV in all areas of the apartments, constantly monitored by a welfare team, with panic buttons and "safe words" in place.She concluded that, with enhancements to the existing welfare framework and adjustments to the format, it would have been reasonable to continue to produce future series of MAFS UK.Speaking to BBC Radio 4's PM programme on Thursday, she added that the suggested changes "would have, in lots of ways, changed both the format and the nature of the show, but would have given the kind of protection that both Channel Four and CPL would have ideally looked for  to ensure the safety of all contributors".But she added that she "completely understood" why Dogra "decided that she doesn't want to proceed with it". The other part of the review, by law firm Clyde & Co, found that Channel 4 and CPL's welfare protocols were compliant with Ofcom's broadcasting code. There were no findings of a breach of the code regarding the handling of issues raised at the relevant times.But it said there were "a small number of instances" where the show's protocols had not been fully applied.This included one incident when "some contributors contravened the Code of Conduct relating to prohibited substances but were given a first and final warning rather than being removed from the programme".It added that Channel 4 and CPL could have undertaken a more structured longer-term review over multiple series. The review also made recommendations for areas where the contributor welfare framework could be "further strengthened". Dogra said welfare across all of their programmes is "a primary concern".She said that considering the "wholesale implementation" of the recommendations "provoked fundamental questions about the editorial proposition of a show that, I believe, has now run its course over 10 years".She added that the review "did not have the authority to adjudicate on the very serious allegations made by three women in the Panorama programme". Billed as a "bold social experiment", Married at First Sight UK - known to many as MAFS - sees single people agree to "marry" total strangers, after meeting for the first time at their mock weddings.The marriages are not legally binding, but viewers see the couples go on honeymoon, before moving in together and navigating their relationships - all while being filmed, almost every day.The UK version, which had been running for 10 seasons, is one of Channel 4's biggest shows, with audience figures often topping three million.Following the Panorama broadcast, Channel 4's chief executive Priya Dogra initially didn't apologise, although she did express her "sympathy" for those who had spoken up.Less than 48 hours later, she changed position, telling reporters she was "deeply sorry" over the women's distress.The impact of the Panorama progamme was swift, and sizeable.Channel 4 launched its external review, all the episodes were taken down from its streaming service, and a major sponsor pulled out.Married at First Sight UK usually starts airing in September, but the new series was put on hold following the revelations in the Panorama.Ofcom has since launched an investigation, and in June, a male cast member was arrested on suspicion of rape.The individual is not being named. The alleged victim is also not being named; anyone who makes an allegation of rape is entitled to anonymity by law.If you have more information about this story, you can reach Noor by email at noor.nanji@bbc.co.uk

schema.headline: Married at First Sight UK cancelled after BBC revealed rape allegations

title: Celtic 3-2 Besiktas: Duran & Osmand spark Celtic into life - but where does that leave Hogh?
description: Image source, SNSImage caption, Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran were key as Celtic turned the game on its headByGeorge O'NeillBBC Sport ScotlandWith an
body: Image source, SNSImage caption, Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran were key as Celtic turned the game on its headByGeorge O'NeillBBC Sport ScotlandWith an hour gone at Parkhead on Thursday, hope in the stands was in short supply.Celtic were 1-0 down against Besiktas and heading towards a fourth straight defeat in this season's Europa League.Manager Martin O'Neill turned to his bench for a spark, bringing on Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran to replace Sebastian Tounekti and James Forrest out wide.The impact was almost instantaneous. Osmand's first touch nestled in the bottom corner of Alexander Nubel's goal, just 43 seconds after the 20-year-old attacker came on.All of a sudden, Celtic had a threat in behind and Besiktas looked rattled.Then, on 77 minutes, O'Neill withdrew Kasper Hogh after another underwhelming display from the club record signing and moved Duran through the middle.Again it had the desired effect.Osmand played Duran through with a delightful pass and the Colombian rounded Nubel before slotting Celtic into the lead.Orkun Kokcu levelled for Besiktas with a fine strike, but Duran had the final say two minutes later, controlling Kieran Tierney's scuffed shot and beating Nubel from close range to send the home support into ecstasy."Everything changed with the subs; Osmand coming on and Duran going through the middle," former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov said on TNT Sports. "They freed up space for Nygren and Baur. It was a really positive 30 minutes."Not since Johannes Edvaldsson against Jeunesse d'Esch in the European Cup in September 1977 had a Celtic substitute scored twice in Europe (excluding qualifiers)."Osmand came on, first touch put the ball in the net and that's really difficult, he can definitely score a goal. Duran has been fabulous for us all season no matter where he plays," O'Neill said of his goalscorers.The Northern Irishman was asked whether it was a case of inspired substitutions or rather evidence that he should have started his best players."I'm not standing up for myself, not at all," he said. "It was in design to do exactly what it did. We've played nine games in 25 days, some players needed a breather and you can get re-energised from coming on the field. "I'm going to say that that was our plan and those players were going to come on the pitch at some point in the game."Figure caption, 'Celtic character shone through big time' - O'NeillNumbers point to Duran as solutionThe contrast between Celtic's attacking play with Hogh leading the line and with Duran through the middle was stark. The £11m Dane's effort cannot be questioned. He continued to battle to  try to make things happen, but since arriving from Bodo/Glimt in the summer, he has now failed to score in 16 of his 17 Celtic appearances.In 77 minutes against Besiktas, he didn't have a single shot and managed just one touch in the opposition box.Duran, meanwhile, played just half an hour and scored two goals, had two shots, and registered four touches in the Besiktas box.O'Neill has previously said he is unsure of his best team, but it is now obvious that Duran is Celtic's best option through the middle.Despite Hogh's price tag, it feels inevitable he will be among the Celtic substitutes for high-stakes games."It'll be tough for Hogh," Hearts defender Craig Halkett said on TNT Sports. "He was the big-money singing but it's not coming off for him."As a player you need to keep your head down, keep working hard and hope it turns."Osmand too appears to have pushed himself to the front of the queue to start off the left. The former Fulham man is direct and evidently has an eye for goal, with a happy knack for scoring in big games."This is a great team we're playing against," Osmand told TNT Sports. "Camilo [Duran] did amazing, he's such a poacher. Credit to him."It's a lot harder starting games. The team dug in, stayed strong and we got our rewards."[The goal] caught me off guard, but I'm just glad I caught it nice. I just want to come on and make something happen. So happy with tonight."Figure caption, Celtic goalscorer Osmand on 'surreal feeling'

schema.headline: Celtic 3-2 Besiktas: Duran & Osmand spark Celtic into life - but where does that leave Hogh?

title: Who could Thomas Tuchel select for next England squad? Lankshear, King, Dewsbury-Hall, Henderson, White, Gibbs-White
description: England have made medical checks on Cole Palmer as Thomas Tuchel considers whether to select the Chelsea forward in his next squad.The 24-year-old mis
body: England have made medical checks on Cole Palmer as Thomas Tuchel considers whether to select the Chelsea forward in his next squad.The 24-year-old missed all four games during the previous international window with a minor injury.He completed 90 minutes for Chelsea against Brentford before those matches, and started for the Blues in the first game afterwards.Tuchel, who names his squad to face Croatia and Spain on Friday, said at the time that Palmer was "playing with discomfort and pain" but was "missing too many opportunities" with England.Whether he is recalled will be a key theme on Friday. While it is normal for England medical staff to check on players under consideration, it also underlines that Palmer remains on Tuchel's radar despite his stark comments in September.In addition to deciding whether to select Palmer, head coach Tuchel has a number of other dilemmas to resolve.Bukayo Saka's injury absence opens the door to another attacker, with his Arsenal team-mate Noni Madueke pushing for a recall following a string of impressive performances.Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has not played since mid-October and is not fit for selection, while Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah is a major injury doubt.Defenders Ben White and Djed Spence are pushing for recalls after missing out on the previous squad through injury.The likes of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice and many others are now stonewall selections - but the intrigue is around the remaining few spots still seemingly up for grabs.Will some old faces earn a recall or will there be new faces soon pulling on the England shirt? BBC Sport runs down some of the potential candidates for selection.There is a lack of number nines in the English game and the job of being Harry Kane's understudy is harder than it sounds.The England captain has just won the Ballon d'Or, likes to play almost every minute for his country and is the captain, record goalscorer and arguably the best player in Tuchel's side.Dominic Calvert-Lewin has been selected in the squads before and since the World Cup but, despite doing well for Leeds, it has not quite clicked for him under Tuchel and he was given just 15 minutes in two substitute appearances in the last window.Tuchel has started to use Bellingham as the back-up to Kane, but he could opt for more of a prospect in his squad in this shorter window and turn to Lankshear.The 21-year-old striker, who like Kane started at Tottenham, was sold to Middlesbrough this summer for £20m and has scored 15 goals in all competitions so far this campaign.He has scored 13 goals in as many games in the Championship, helping Middlesbrough to the top of the division.He only made his debut for the England Under-21s during the last international window and scored in that game so it would be quite a rise for a player who is not in the Premier League.Tuchel is aware of Lankshear and with a lack of number nines across the age groups it could be an interesting option for a manager who is not afraid of making big calls.He did miss Middlesbrough's loss to Wrexham on Wednesday with a tweaked hamstring but could return in time for Saturday.

schema.headline: Who could Thomas Tuchel select for next England squad? Lankshear, King, Dewsbury-Hall, Henderson, White, Gibbs-White

title: Police car set alight in Glasgow amid Bonfire Night trouble
description: Figure caption, Police vehicle set alight after officers targeted in GlasgowByMegan Bonar and Yana Thandrayen BBC ScotlandUpdated 24 minutes agoSeven
body: Figure caption, Police vehicle set alight after officers targeted in GlasgowByMegan Bonar and Yana Thandrayen BBC ScotlandUpdated 24 minutes agoSeven people have been arrested during Bonfire Night disorder in parts of Scotland, police say.A police officer and an ambulance staff member sustained minor injuries when they were attacked with fireworks while responding to a report of an injured man in Glasgow, according to Police Scotland.         A police vehicle was set alight and seriously damaged during the incident in the Greenside Street area, and a 16-year-old boy was arrested.Police and members of the public were also targeted with fireworks in several areas of Edinburgh.Fire service personnel came under attack in a number of towns while responding to calls but none were hurt and no serious damage was caused to fire engines."Police officers, ambulance staff and firefighters are there to protect communities – not be the target of violence," Chief Superintendent David Robertson said. "I want to make it clear that thorough investigations will now take place to identify those responsible and bring them to justice."He added that the policing operation covering the Halloween and Bonfire Night had been "one of the most complex and demanding deployments in recent memory involving the largest number of officers" since the visit of US President Donald Trump last year. However, there had been a "reduction in serious incidents requiring... specialist resources" compared with the same period last year, he added.Police Scotland said they had received reports of youths "creating a blockage in the road" on Oxgangs Road North, Edinburgh, at about 17:30.A spokesperson said: "Officers attended and fireworks were set off in their direction, but no injuries have been reported."Several small fires in bins and the park were extinguished by the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service."In Wester Hailes, the fire service attended a fire in a grass area near houses in Murrayburn Park.Firefighters were called to the scene of a bonfire shortly after 19:00, with one fire engine called out to extinguish the flames.Figure caption, Fireworks at Cardonald Park, GlasgowFireworks were also thrown at a fire appliance in Knightswood in Glasgow, while in Dundee, a public order unit was deployed after more than 100 young people gathered and started a fire on the road.Reports suggest a crowd of approximately 50 people were launching fireworks and causing disorder.A 15-year-old was taken to hospital in Alexandria after lighting a firework that exploded and damaged his eye.Fire crews were also attacked in Castlemilk, Whitburn and Cumnock.Image caption, Officers watched over disorder from a command centre in EdinburghBBC Scotland was given access to the Strategic co-ordination centre at the Police HQ at Fettes.A wall of CCTV cameras trained across Edinburgh and Glasgow flickered from empty streets to a packed Celtic stadium as officers watch for signs of disorder.The atmosphere in the room was calm despite pockets of disorder - things seemed generally under control.Information flashed up on screens with updates from Operation Moonbeam. As the evening progressed the screens filled up as public order units were deployed to more and more places.Teams from Police Scotland, Scottish Fire and Rescue Service, Scottish Ambulance Service, the Scottish government and Edinburgh city council were in attendance.Officers from as far afield as Avon and Somerset, Hampshire, Hertfordshire and South Wales were ready to be deployed.Additional reporting by Paul Ward and Patrick Jackson.

schema.headline: Police car set alight in Glasgow amid Bonfire Night trouble

title: White House denies Hegseth, Rubio will leave jobs amid Republican election fallout
description: Meanwhile, Rubio is denying reports he is considering leaving his post ahead of a 2028 presidential run.Working for Trump until the end of his term ha
body: Meanwhile, Rubio is denying reports he is considering leaving his post ahead of a 2028 presidential run.Working for Trump until the end of his term has "always been my plan," Rubio told The New York Times in an interview."I love the work I'm doing," Rubio said. "And plus I always laugh when they say he's going to leave his job. I go, 'Which one?'"The White House and US State Department also shut down reports that Rubio might be leaving after this week's midterm losses, with both calling it "fake news".The defence secretary, though, faces a more uncertain political future. Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have both blamed the Iran war for Republican losses that allowed Democrats full control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate. In a telephone interview with ABC News, Trump said that he had received "calls about" Hegseth, but added that he had  "every intention" of keeping him.Later on Thursday, he told reporters at the White House that "Pete Hegseth has done a fantastic job", and went on to list what he sees are some of his achievements, including the arrest of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro in January and the Iran war, now into its ninth month.

schema.headline: White House denies Hegseth, Rubio will leave jobs amid Republican election fallout

title: British doctor infected with Ebola in DR Congo being treated at London hospital
description: Image caption, A large convoy of emergency vehicles transported the man to the Royal Free Hospital in north LondonA British doctor who tested positive
body: Image caption, A large convoy of emergency vehicles transported the man to the Royal Free Hospital in north LondonA British doctor who tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown back to the UK.The man, who has not been identified, landed at RAF Northolt before being transported to a specialist infectious diseases unit at the Royal Free Hospital in north London.It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.Dr Renu Bindra, deputy director of the All Hazards Public Health Response team at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), said there are "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and the risk to the public remains low.The infected doctor was brought to the UK on a medical evacuation flight as part of a joint effort by the UK and DR Congo governments and their international health partners, the Department of Health (DoH) said. A convoy of emergency vehicles were on hand to complete the transfer following the man's arrival at the RAF base. Three large police vans travelled at either end of the convoy, while two ambulances and another support car were involved.Traffic was stopped and police exited the vans to keep the public away as the convoy arrived at the Royal Free Hospital. The man is now being treated in a "highly specialised"  isolation unit at the hospital, the DoH said. Image source, ReutersThe Royal Free Hospital successfully treated three health workers who had been evacuated after the Ebola outbreak in West Africa in 2014 and 2015.There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.None of these cases have resulted in a death. Image caption, The plane carrying the infected man arrived at RAF Northolt on ThursdayThere have been more than 10,000 confirmed cases since the recent outbreak in DR Congo started in May, which has grown to become the second most deadly recorded spate of infections, behind the outbreak in West Africa in the 2010s.The current outbreak in DR Congo has a fatality rate of 48.6% reported at the end of last month.Ebola can result in serious illness and death. Early symptoms include vomiting and diarrhoea but it can progress to organ failure and internal bleeding.The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.The ongoing outbreak centred on DR Congo is fuelled by the Bundibugyo variant of the virus.There is no approved vaccine but the World Health Organization said experts have recommended adding two new candidate drugs to an ongoing clinical trial.The vaccines, one developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and another by the firm Moderna, will join the trial once they are approved by Congolese health authorities.It will be the first time jabs specifically designed to protect against the Bundibugyo virus are tested during an outbreak.Since the outbreak, Ebola cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

schema.headline: British doctor infected with Ebola in DR Congo being treated at London hospital

title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
description: Hundreds of billions of dollars in market value has been wiped from major tech firms in the US and Asia in a stock market rout after the US midterm el
body: Hundreds of billions of dollars in market value has been wiped from major tech firms in the US and Asia in a stock market rout after the US midterm elections sparked concerns of a slowdown in artificial intelligence development.Shares in firms across the tech and AI sectors plummeted following Democratic wins after election campaigns run on slowing AI.The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index closed down by more than 5.5%, losing an estimated $2.5tn (£1.9tn) in market value, according to Dow Jones data, while other key US stock indexes also saw big losses in their worst days since 2025.The sell-off comes on top of broader concerns about whether the huge amounts being spent on AI will pay off.In Asia, tech-heavy indexes fell sharply on Friday morning as firms that make the computer chips and other equipment that power AI saw their shares slide.The Nikkei 225 in Japan was 6% lower in early trading as shares in memory chip maker Kioxia lost over 12.6% and rival Tokyo Electron slipped by 9.5%.South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix fell by more than 11.5%, while Samsung was down by nearly 10%.The sell-off in Seoul sent the Kospi index plunging more than 8.5%, triggering a so-called circuit breaker, a mechanism that temporarily halts trading to curb panic selling.Taiwan's Taiex dropped by more than 8.3%, with chipmaking giant TSMC falling by nearly 8.5%.It marks a "continuation of worries" over the level of spending on AI infrastructure, said MarketWatch chips analyst Britney Nguyen.Democrats in races across the US campaigned to slow the growth of data centres and AI, and there were dozens of measures on ballots around the country aimed at restricting the development of the hubs crucial for powering the technology.They won both the US Senate and House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterms, taking control of Congress for the rest of President Donald Trump's presidency.Texas' Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector.Live: What can Democrats do with control of Congress? We answer your US midterms questionsFood, fuel and taxes – can the Democrats actually make life cheaper?Boebert, billionaires' tax and other midterms races still to watchIn a social media post, Trump blamed the slide on his political opponents."The Stock Market suffered one of the Worst Days in History based on the results of the Election," he said."Remember, it wasn't Republicans, it was Dumocrats. Do not fear, however, we will soon, one way or the other, be BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN!"Some Democrats have argued that AI has grown too big without any safeguards or oversight and have promised, with their new power in Congress, to change that."Americans don't want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment, gutting jobs and threatening humanity's future. NATIONAL DATA CENTER MORATORIUM NOW," Democrat Senator Bernie Sanders said in a post on X on Thursday.Shares in companies heavily exposed to AI data centres, including crucial chipmakers and semiconductor manufacturers, fell sharply on Thursday, highlighting investor concerns that had already been growing.In European trading on Thursday, shares in chipmaker Infineon fell by more than 8.5% while tech equipment manufacturer ASML dropped by 6.5%.Nvidia shares slid more than 9%, knocking more than $400bn off the firm's market value in New York trading.Other chipmakers also suffered, with AMD and Micron both dropping by more than 17%. Intel shares also dropped, down 10.3%, while memory card maker SanDisk plunged more than 22%.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks the performance of 30 of the largest companies involved in semiconductor production, fell by more than 12%.Shares in Elon Musk's companies SpaceX and Tesla also plunged, falling 8% and nearly 11% respectively and shaving more than $300bn off the firms' market value on Thursday.Musk had spent nearly $450m backing Republican campaigns, including at least $45m in support of Ken Paxton for the Texas senate seat, but Texas was turned blue in the Democratic tsunami on Tuesday night.In total, the so-called magnificent seven tech companies, including Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, have shed a trillion dollars in value in a single trading day.The stock falls also hit other major US stock indexes. The S&P 500 index fell by 4.4% by the end of trading, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average erased gains made on Wednesday to close down more than 3.4%.The Nasdaq Composite fall was so large it is now in what market watchers call correction territory, which is where an index or company value falls at least 10% below its recent high.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said the steep sell-off on the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 was sending shockwaves into other markets."Fresh panic over the AI trade has hit Wall Street hard," she said."Fears that the vast sums poured into AI infrastructure may not deliver the returns investors have been banking on are now colliding with the prospect of a sharp slowdown in data centre construction."Greater scrutiny of data centre approvals, and their impact on the environment and electricity bills could delay projects and raise costs across the industry, said Charu Chanana, Chief Investment Strategist at Saxo. While both political parties are keen to ensure the US' dominance in the technology, "there is a difference between supporting AI development and allowing infrastructure to expand at any cost or pace," she said.Some tech leaders have said they were caught off guard by the backlash against data centres in the midterms.OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman said he believed everyone had been surprised by the reaction to data centres, and more work needed to be done to ensure communities were on board."A lot of our shift over the course of this year has really been to realise that from San Francisco trying to build infrastructure in Texas, Georgia, and other places, you can't just tweet and say: 'This is going to be good.' You need to be in those communities," Brockman said at the WSJ Tech conference in Napa, California on Wednesday evening.Meta's president Dina Powell McCormick said that the industry needed to put more effort into selling AI as a good idea."I think we need to double and triple down on telling the story," she told the WSJ conference.Alongside the immediate impacts of the US mid-term elections, some investors have become concerned that AI shares could be in a bubble that is due a correction.With additional reporting from Lily Jamali

schema.headline: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
